We build models, analytics, and measurement frameworks that enable vehicle detection, entity resolution, behavioral insights, fraud and theft indicators, compliance signals, and network-wide operational performance metrics. Our work sits at the center of the freight intelligence platform, shaping how billions of roadside observations become actionable information. desc: A healthier future. It’s what drives us to innovate. To continuously advance science and ensure everyone has access to the healthcare they need today and for generations to come. Creating a world where we all have more time with the people we love. That’s what makes us Roche. Advances in AI, data, and computational sciences are transforming drug discovery and development. Roche’s Research and Early Development organisations at Genentech (gRED) and Pharma (pRED) have demonstrated how these technologies accelerate R&D, leveraging data and novel computational models to drive impact. Seamless data sharing and access to models across gRED and pRED are essential to maximising these opportunities. We are seeking a Senior Machine Learning Scientist to join the Foundation Models team within Prescient Design (gRED). In this role, you will drive the development of our internal reasoning Large Language Models (LLMs) and enable them to succeed at drug discovery tasks, including biomolecular design. You will work at the intersection of engineering and research, designing and scaling large machine learning systems. In this role, you will: Technical Leadership & Strategy: Lead the design and evolution of scientific reasoning systems, setting technical direction for model architectures, training strategies, and evaluation methodologies. Model Capability & Improvement: Define and execute approaches to systematically improve model performance on scientific tasks, including long-horizon reasoning and complex decision-making. Domain Translation: Translate biological and chemical domain knowledge into machine learning objectives, training signals, and evaluation criteria, working closely with domain experts. Scalable Systems & Engineering: Architect and improve large-scale distributed machine learning systems, ensuring robustness, efficiency, and reproducibility across training and evaluation workflows. Research-to-Production Impact: Partner with researchers and cross-functional teams to move models from research prototypes to production-ready systems that support active discovery programs. As a Senior ML Scientist: You are the primary driver of technical implementation for scientific reasoning, translating high-level research goals into robust training code. You own the end-to-end integrity of large-scale training runs, from data orchestration to the development of rigorous reasoning benchmarks. You act as a technical mentor to junior staff and interns, fostering a culture of engineering excellence and rapid experimentation. Experience: 0–2+ years of industry or postdoctoral experience with a focus on deep learning. LLM Expertise: Extensive experience developing and training large-scale machine learning models, including approaches to improve domain understanding, reasoning capabilities, and model alignment. Publication Record: A strong history of research excellence at top-tier venues (e.g., NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML). Engineering: Strong software engineering skills and experience designing and operating large-scale or high-performance machine learning systems. Preferred Experience with molecular modalities (e.g., protein sequences, chemical graphs, and structured molecular data) is highly valued but not required. A public portfolio of research or significant contributions to open-source ML libraries. A passion for applying frontier AI to drug discovery. desc: About the Opportunity About the Institute Do you want to be part of an exciting new Institute focused on combining human and machine intelligence into working AI solutions? We are building a pioneering research and innovation hub in AI—one that will shape the way humans and machines collaborate for decades to come. Led by Prof. Samuel V. Scarpino, the Institute for Experiential AI is built around the challenges and opportunities made possible by human-machine collaboration. The Institute provides a framework to design, implement, and scale AI-driven technologies in ways that make a true difference to society. Our ability to respond to the opportunities afforded to society will depend on training and building a workforce that is AI-capable and prosperous. Founded in 1898, Northeastern is a global research university and the recognized leader in experience-driven lifelong learning. Our world-renowned experiential approach empowers our students, faculty, alumni, and partners to create impact far beyond the confines of discipline, degree, and campus. The Culture Here at the Institute for Experiential AI (EAI) we are committed to the highest standards in all we do. Working at the EAI offers opportunities, an environment, and a culture that just isn’t found together anywhere else. This is the right place for you if you’re curious, motivated by the future of technology, and want to be part of a unique and diverse community that works on high-impact research, educational, business, and societal problems. Position Summary Northeastern University's Institute for Experiential AI is opening an ML engineer with special focus on physical AI systems, knowledge aggregation and AI for control and optimization for a DOE Genesis project led by Dr. Ayan Paul. The ML Engineer will be based at the Boston campus, MA, conduct applied research, prepare work for submission to journal/conference publications, and contribute to extramural funding applications. The ML Engineer will work on projects that will include developing AI models for signal processing. Participation in this project will include scientific programming, data analysis, training AI models, manuscript preparation, meeting with collaborators, mentoring graduate students, etc. About the project: CLARA (Cognitive Layered Agentic Reasoning for ARIS) is a three-year, Genesis Mission Phase II project led by Northeastern University with MSU/FRIB and Gravitate AI. It will build an agentic AI system for operating the Advanced Rare Isotope Separator (ARIS) at FRIB. ARIS operations are limited by the gap between LISE++ simulations and observed beam behavior. As a result, weekly beam development takes 16 to 24 hours, about half of which goes to manual isotope calibration. Planning a new experiment takes about 20 days, and no predictive monitoring exists for roughly 200 time-correlated machine parameters. CLARA addresses this with three objectives: Planning and tuning. Bayesian optimization uses LISE++ as a physics-informed prior, alongside paired forward and inverse neural surrogates trained on simulation and EPICS archive data. These power a Planning Agent for non-experts and an Expert Tuning Agent. Calibration. Diffeomorphic image registration maps simulated particle identification (PID) distributions to measured ones from a single measurement. Monitoring and knowledge. title: Quantitative Developer

desc:
About the role

Teza has built a new intent generation platform and strategy building framework for mid-frequency trading, written in-house from scratch. It is the layer that turns research into production strategies: the framework defines how a strategy is expressed, the platform computes target positions and generates trading intents.



One strategy already trades on the platform in production at seconds-scale frequency. Next, all of our existing strategies move onto it, and completely new strategies get built directly on top of it. This role is central to that effort.



Your job is to implement strategies on the platform, build the data pipelines that feed them, and implement the execution algorithms that trade them. The role covers the whole path from raw data to orders in the market, and you own the full lifecycle: the engineer who implements a strategy also understands, and often builds, its upstream data and downstream execution.



The data our strategies trade on, by the numbers:

 - 3 PB of historical market data, growing by 1.5 TB compressed every day

 - 1 PB of raw historical vendor data, growing by ~150 GB every day

 - 120 TB of processed, query-ready data in historical storage

 - Thousands of scheduled jobs: run by cron today, actively migrating to Apache Airflow

 - Alternative data delivered directly into the real-time feeds of live trading strategies

The firm is looking for outstanding technical skills, strong attention to detail, and a desire to own strategies end to end, from the data they read to the orders they send.



Location

Austin, TX / Yerevan, Armenia (in-office requirement)



Key Responsibilities

 - Implement strategies on the new framework: migrate the existing ones, validating behavioral parity for each one, and build completely new ones.

 - Work directly with Portfolio Managers and Quantitative Researchers: turn their research into production strategies, and serve as the authority on how those strategies compute and trade.

 - Implement execution algorithms that turn a strategy's intents into orders, and measure their execution quality.

 - Design and onboard new data sources into our warehouse, and build the pipelines that deliver them to research and to live strategies.

 - Build automated systems for data cleansing, anomaly detection, monitoring, and alerting, ensuring bad data never reaches a strategy.

 - Shape the framework through the strategies you build on it: identify bottlenecks and friction points, and spearhead the necessary enhancements.

 - Support your strategies, pipelines, and execution algorithms in production, where they trade real capital.



What we're building right now

 - Migration of all existing strategies onto the new platform, alongside completely new strategies built natively on it.

 - Execution algorithms for the strategies running on the platform.

 - Core framework capabilities underpinning the strategies you implement: parallel compute, data locality, and caching of intermediate results across strategies, backtests, and live runs.

 - A bitemporal data store, designed and written in-house from scratch. Every dataset answers both "what did we know then?" and "what do we know now?", which is what lets researchers trust a backtest.

 - A Python 3.14 migration of a large, long-lived codebase.

 - Adoption of the latest Apache Airflow: writing DAGs for the thousands of jobs moving off cron.

 - Pipelines for market data and alternative data: everything from exchange feeds to weather.

 - Real-time delivery: alternative data flows straight into strategies' live feeds. Your work is part of the live trading path.

 - CI/CD for all of it, in GitHub Actions.



Our Stack

Python and Java · Apache Airflow · Slurm · NATS · PostgreSQL · MongoDB · S3 · NFS · GitHub Actions



Basic Requirements

 - Strong software engineering in Python on Unix/Linux, with a track record of shipping production code that others depend on.

 - Experience implementing quantitative models or trading strategies in code, and making numerical, data-intensive code correct and fast.

 - Experience building and running data pipelines: ingestion, cleaning, scheduling, and monitoring.

 - Strong SQL, including query optimization and performance tuning, and a solid grasp of data modeling.

 - Comfort working with large time-series datasets, and the rigor to prevent look-ahead bias.

 - Solid computer science fundamentals: data structures and algorithms.



Nice to have

 - Experience at a systematic trading firm, implementing strategies inside a backtesting or strategy framework.

 - Experience implementing execution algorithms, and familiarity with market microstructure, order types, and transaction cost analysis.

 - Java (part of our platform is written in it).

 - Apache Airflow or similar workflow orchestration tools.

 - Experience with Slurm or another HPC scheduler.

 - Experience with on-premises data infrastructure.



Benefits

 - Health, vision and dental insurance

 - Flexible sick time policy

The successful candidate will develop and own quantitative models used to assess battery dispatch, revenues and economics. The candidate will use models to analyze battery storage market opportunities and how they are evolving across global power markets. The rapid deployment of battery storage is changing the way power markets operate. Understanding the value of storage requires increasingly sophisticated modeling of asset operation, electricity prices, market participation and interactions between growing storage capacity and the wider power system. BNEF is a strategic research provider covering global commodity markets and the disruptive technologies driving the transition to a low-carbon economy. Our expert coverage assesses pathways for the power, transport, industry, buildings and agriculture sectors to adapt to the energy transition. We help commodity trading, corporate strategy, finance and policy professionals navigate change and generate opportunities. The Solar & Energy Storage team covers the technologies, markets and economics shaping the sector globally. We forecast storage deployment and battery costs, track projects and market activity, assess policy and regulatory developments, and analyze the investment case for storage across different markets and applications. This includes quantitative modelling to understand battery dispatch and revenues, the impact of storage penetration on power markets, and the value of storage across different durations, technologies and market designs. desc: 2027 Summer Intern - AI for Drug Discovery Department Summary The Foundation Models team is seeking exceptional graduate interns with strong research experience in machine learning (ML) and a passion for applying advanced algorithms to scientific discovery. Our team develops state-of-the-art generative models, autonomous scientific agents, and foundational ML methods to accelerate drug design. Autonomous agents increasingly run long scientific workflows in which they must decide, round after round, whether to continue a promising strategy, explore a new one, stop an unproductive experiment, or revisit an earlier hypothesis. Yet we know little about whether these agents learn from experimental evidence the way a good scientist would. This internship will study that question rigorously, using real multi-round drug discovery campaigns. The intern will test whether agents make decisions for the right scientific reasons: whether they learn across rounds, distinguish strong evidence from weak or confounded evidence, and account for epistemic uncertainty from limited knowledge and aleatoric uncertainty from inherent outcome variability. They will also study how different representations of prior experience (raw history, compaction, structured summaries, self-reflection) shape this behavior. A central open question is which failures can be addressed through how evidence is presented to the agent, and which require changing the model itself through post-training, and how to tell the two apart in a principled way. Intern candidates should have a strong interest in LLM agents, evaluation methodology, decision-making under uncertainty, and post-training. The ideal intern is comfortable conducting independent research, rapidly prototyping ideas, and collaborating with multidisciplinary scientists. This internship position is located in South San Francisco, on-site. The Opportunity Design and build a benchmark of real and controlled counterfactual decision points from multi-round scientific design campaigns Develop quantitative metrics for decision quality under varying evidence strength, uncertainty, and cost Characterize recurring agent failure modes and develop a principled method for deciding whether each is best addressed through harness or context changes or through post-training Explore post-training (e.g., supervised fine-tuning on historical trajectories and counterfactual examples) of smaller specialized models, and compare against prompting and context-engineering baselines on held-out targets Develop well-documented, reproducible evaluation and training code and curated datasets, and present results for potential publication at internal or external scientific conferences or workshops. title: Research Scientist – Recursive Self-Improvement
location: Sunnyvale, CA Sunnyvale, CA US
desc:
About the Institute of Foundation Models
The Institute of Foundation Models is a research lab at Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence (MBZUAI) dedicated to building, understanding, and responsibly deploying foundation models. Our researchers and engineers work across model training, evaluation, and systems. We share our work through publications, technical reports, and open-source releases, and help train the next generation of AI researchers and builders.
 The Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) team studies how foundation models can contribute to training and evaluating their successors. A model might construct a coding task, write a verifier, or use execution feedback to revise a solution. The research question is whether those contributions improve the next model’s ability to solve unfamiliar problems, and whether that model can, in turn, produce better training tasks and feedback. As a Research Scientist, you will shape this research agenda and lead projects from an initial hypothesis through large-scale experiments. You will design learning algorithms, build environments that provide meaningful feedback, and study how gains and errors accumulate over successive training rounds. The role combines independent research with hands-on engineering across data generation, post-training, and evaluation. Develop algorithms for recursive self-improvement. Design and test methods for models to propose tasks, attempt solutions, learn from feedback, and select experiences for subsequent training rounds. Build tasks and environments with verifiable outcomes. Develop agentic tasks in domains such as coding, program analysis, and tool use. Design execution-based verifiers and investigate what happens when a verifier accepts an incorrect solution or rejects a valid one. Study how to select training data as models improve. Investigate which tasks produce the greatest learning gains at each stage of training and how to maintain coverage as earlier tasks become easier. Measure improvement across generations. Design held-out evaluations, ablations, and compute-matched baselines that isolate the contribution of model-generated tasks and feedback. Diagnose failure modes such as reward hacking, declining task diversity, and errors that compound across rounds. Scale promising methods. Work with research engineers to integrate generation, verification, and training into distributed post-training systems. Quantify the trade-offs among model capability, feedback quality, and computational cost. Communicate and share research. Publish findings, contribute reproducible code and evaluations for public release, and build collaborations within MBZUAI and across the research community. MSc, MEng, or PhD in machine learning, computer science, or a related field, or equivalent research experience. Compensation
$150,000 – $450,000/year + discretionary performance bonus + benefits

The actual base compensation offered may vary within this range depending on individual qualifications, including but not limited to relevant skills, experience, education, certifications, and specific business needs. In addition to base salary, total compensation includes an annual discretionary performance bonus and comprehensive benefits.
Benefits Include
Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision benefits
Bonus
401K Plan
Generous paid time off, sick leave and holidays
Paid Parental Leave
Employee Assistance Program
Life insurance and disability
Professional Experience
Minimum
Three or more years of hands-on research experience in machine learning, including substantial work in reinforcement learning, foundation model post-training, program synthesis, or learning from model-generated data.
Experience independently formulating a research question, implementing a method, and designing experiments that distinguish among plausible explanations for a result.
Strong Python skills and experience implementing learning algorithms or evaluation pipelines in a deep learning framework such as PyTorch or JAX.
Practical experience training or evaluating models using feedback from an environment, a verifier, human supervision, or another model.
Demonstrated research or engineering contributions through publications, technical reports, open-source software, or deployed systems.
Ability to communicate findings clearly and collaborate with researchers and engineers across disciplines.
Preferred Skills
Experience with self-play, curriculum learning, meta-RL, expert iteration, or iterative training on synthetic data.
Experience building coding agents, executable task environments, programmatic verifiers, or formal verification tools.
Familiarity with reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards, reward modeling, or learning under noisy or systematically biased feedback.
Experience evaluating multi-step agents, detecting benchmark contamination, or measuring generalization to unfamiliar tasks.
Experience running distributed training or inference on large clusters and diagnosing bottlenecks across rollout generation, environment execution, and optimization.
A record of publications in leading machine learning venues or contributions to widely used open-source training and evaluation tools.
